manifest.name: @local/dsh-session-auto-resume
manifest.description: Automatically resumes DeepSeek Harness sessions interrupted by app closure: active-goal sessions re-arm and continue their round budget at next launch; mid-turn non-goal sessions are detected and logged for one-click resume.

bundle.text:
# Session-auto-resume bundle. Mounts one host-plane plugin that closes the
# no-startup-recovery gap: after ANY host closure (crash, SIGTERM, deliberate
# quit/reload) interrupted sessions stay interrupted until a human acts
# (verified 2026-10-19: dsh-desktop-host has quit-time inspection only, and
# dsh-goal-round-driver "never revives work on its own").
#
# At boot (+settleMs) the plugin scans recent persisted sessions and:
#   - durable goal phase=active  -> explicit resume (agents.resume +
#     goals.resume re-arm; the mounted goal-round-driver then continues the
#     round budget automatically). Paused/blocked goals are NEVER re-armed —
#     those are deliberate human states.
#   - open turn without a goal   -> detected + logged for one-click GUI resume.
#   - clean / stale / live       -> skipped.
#
# DELIVERY NOTE (2026-10-19): the row below is the part that makes the mount
# real — a bundles-list entry alone is silently skipped by the running host
# (the trap documented in @local/dsh-host-exit-marker commit b7e15fc and
# upstream as deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness Discussions #10022).
#
# dryRun was TRUE for first delivery (spec dsh-auto-session-resume-spec-
# 2026-10-19.md, DoD D5). D5 CLOSED 2026-10-19: the pass ran live in the
# running host (activated by the profile's live bundle reload — no restart
# needed) and its verdicts on 30 real persisted sessions matched an
# independently derived classification of the same logs (0 resume-worthy,
# 0 surface-worthy; the only active-goal session is the live one, correctly
# skip-live; the two false-positive greps were a completed goal and a
# non-goal "phase" field). dryRun is now FALSE: the next host closure with
# active goal work gets the explicit resume + re-arm.
- insert:
    - id: session-auto-resume
      name: '@local/dsh-session-auto-resume'
      config:
        dryRun: false
        maxResumesPerBoot: 3
        staleWindowHours: 48
        scanLimit: 30
        settleMs: 5000

readme.text: A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that **automatically resumes agent sessions interrupted by app closure**. When the DSH host relaunches, sessions that were mid-work at closure are detected from persisted state and recovered without human action:

- **Sessions with an active goal** are explicitly resumed and the goal re-armed — after which the bundled [`goal-round-driver`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/goal/goal-round-driver) continues the round budget automatically. (The driver deliberately "never revives work on its own"; this plugin performs the explicit resume the driver requires.)
- **Mid-turn sessions without a goal** are detected and logged with a ready-to-run resume command — surfaced, never auto-worked.
- Cleanly-ended, stale (>48 h), live, and subagent-owned sessions are skipped. Per-boot resume cap. Fail-closed on goal transitions. Never-throw activation.

The desktop host has quit-time inspection of active work but **no startup recovery path**: after any closure (crash, SIGTERM, deliberate quit/reload), interrupted sessions stay interrupted until a human notices. This plugin closes that gap entirely outside the app bundle, so it survives app updates.
Tested against a real closure-then-relaunch cycle (operator-approved SIGTERM of the running host; app relaunched):

- An **unscripted** interrupted goal session (not planted, not known to the operator) was auto-resumed and its goal re-armed at boot; the round driver then continued the session.
- A session holding an active goal continued on an automatic continuation round with **no human message**.
- Round budgets advanced correctly; a live session was correctly skipped; 489 subagent-owned sessions were correctly excluded in one pass.

`verify-d1.mjs` (included) turns any future closure into a one-command verdict: `PASS` (exit 0) / `FAIL` (exit 1, names the broken check + evidence tail) / `VOID` (exit 2, no closure recorded after the plugin armed). Its own fixture selftest (`verify-d1.test.mjs`) exercises every verdict path against synthetic evidence trees.

- **Policy is explicit and minimal**: only durable goal phase `active` auto-resumes; paused/blocked goals are deliberate human states and are never re-armed; non-goal sessions are surfaced only. The plugin's installation *is* the one-time authorization.
- **Resume mirrors the harness's own resume flow** (`agents.resume({resumeSessionId, agentOptions, setup})` + `goals.resume(agent, {id, revision})`), including binding the default model — a resume without a model binding produces turns failing with `prompt variable "{{model}}" has no value` (the agent loop binds that variable from `agent.options`). This plugin binds it and logs a loud `resume-no-model` line if it cannot.
- **It never hand-appends to session logs.** Session-log append contracts (`headerSeq` must reference an earlier request/header) make cold-log markers unsafe; detection is recorded in the plugin's own log instead.
- **Fail-closed everywhere**: goal resume throws on exhausted budgets or invalid phase transitions (caught, logged, never retried); the boot pass, classification, logging, and resume are each guarded so a plugin failure cannot block host boot.

1. Copy this package to `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-auto-resume`.
2. Link it into your profile's dependencies and add it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list:

```json
   "dependencies": { "@local/dsh-session-auto-resume": "link:/Users/you/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-auto-resume" },
   "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@local/dsh-session-auto-resume" ] } }
   ```

3. The package's own `cordis.patch.yml` carries the required insert row (a bundles-list entry alone is silently skipped). It ships with `dryRun: true` — the first boot logs `would-resume` decisions without acting; verify them against your live sessions, then set `dryRun: false`.
4. Restart the app. Evidence lands in `~/.dsh/logs/session-auto-resume.log` (`ARMED` on every activation, one `pass-done` per boot).

```sh
node selftest.mjs        # classification truth table, fake-ctx passes, mutation checks
node verify-d1.test.mjs  # proves verify-d1 on every verdict path (synthetic fixtures)
```

- Selftest: all legs green under the app runtime (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`).
- Live fire: one real closure-recovery verified end to end; one defect found and fixed during it (the model binding above).
- Known limitation: sessions are matched against the most recent 30 persisted sessions by creation time (config `scanLimit`), and the mechanism mounts at boot only (no hot reload of plugin-file changes).
